scenes.say: Every Friday, platforms pay hundreds of contractors through PayPal Payouts.
The median company loses about one and a half percent of its disbursements to duplicate or wrong payments. That is A P Q C, twenty twenty four. This week's run has a scammer in it.
This is built for finance operations at agencies and marketplaces, the people who pay contractors through PayPal Payouts. Eight documents came in this week.
I'll run the audit. Every invoice is checked against the contract, the payee list, and the payment history.
Eight verdicts come back. Five are clean. Three are exceptions, and each one names the clause it failed.
Start with the biggest one. Tom's invoice asks to be paid at a new address, and the request arrived by email, from a look-alike domain.
No payee change is on file, so clause five quarantines the payee. Nine thousand four hundred dollars, held.
Next, the same October blog series, billed a second time. The invoice number gained a zero, but clause three still catches the duplicate.
Priya's invoice is mostly right. Her hours and her rate check out. But a six hundred and fifty dollar rush surcharge has no written approval, so clause four point three short pays it.
Twenty five thousand, five hundred and eighty dollars billed this week. Fourteen thousand and ninety of it is payable.
Now the payout. One click sends a single PayPal Payouts batch, carrying only the invoices that passed.
That is a real batch id from the PayPal Payouts API. Six items, each one carrying its own remittance note.
PayPal's webhooks report back, and every item turns to success. Fourteen thousand and ninety dollars paid, in one batch. Eleven thousand four hundred and ninety stopped before it left.
Then Priya replies. Her project manager approved the rush in writing, and the message is dated before the work started.
The audit reads that reply against clause four point three, accepts it, and releases a six hundred and fifty dollar top up. A second real batch.
Not a blocker. A fair auditor. Ten thousand eight hundred and forty dollars protected.
PayPal moves the money. PayoutGuard makes sure it is the right amount, to the right person.
Built with OpenAI, PayPal Payouts and webhooks. Synthetic data, on the PayPal sandbox.
